findings.claim: The round-one fix still violates AC1's unconditional 404 requirement for unknown window and comparison IDs.
findings.evidence: windowSources includes windows/<body>.json for every ID without checking membership, and windowHandler:98-104 returns 501 whenever that list is nonempty. comparisonSources in compare.ts:41-44 likewise treats that file as a source for both arbitrary IDs, leading to 501 at lines 85-92. By inspection, a checksum-correct top-N file containing none of the requested IDs still makes /windows/missing and /compare?a=missing&b=other return 501. windows.test.ts:57 and compare.test.ts:98 pin file-presence behavior instead of distinguishing present and absent records within a listed file. The original examples are fixed, but codex-r1-1 and claude-r1-2 remain partially unresolved. The missing schema explains the limitation; it requires an approved contract decision rather than silently narrowing the unknown-ID requirement.

resolution.reason: Fixed in 7fea61d against AC0 as amended by the orchestrator (option a, prd.json notes, 2026-11-14T21:07:20Z). AC0 no longer asks for an unconditional 404 for unknown ids. It asks for 404 where manifest.json rules an id out, and for 501 problem+json naming the missing record schema where only a listed file without a schema (windows/<body>.json, comparisons/<target_id>.json) could resolve the id, because PRD 8.5 and T15-01 forbid parsing those files. The behaviour this finding describes (windows.ts windowSources and windowHandler, compare.ts comparisonSources and compareHandler) is that rule, so no handler changed. As the decision asks, 7fea61d adds a paired test to unavailable.test.ts. It builds two release manifests with the same targets (none of the requested ids), targets.json and comparisons/<other>.json, which differ only in listing windows/earth.json, and a test asserts that difference. Without that file, /windows/test-window-alpha and /compare?a=test-window-alpha&b=test-window-beta give 404 with a detail saying not in bundle <bundle_version>. With it, both give 501 naming windows/earth.json and the missing WindowRecord or ComparisonRecord schema, without passing the file bytes through. /targets/{id} and matches stay 404 for the unlisted target either way. Mutations, each written back afterwards, all fail the new tests: option (c) (top-N file only for listed targets), top-N files ignored, targets.json holding any window, and a 501 detail without the schema name. d4d80a1 adds the amended rule and the t15b-api follow-up to the rule comment in unavailable.ts. t15b-api T15B-02, T15B-03 and T15B-05 replace these 501s once WindowRecord and ComparisonRecord exist.
